title: Забастовка в финале  (A Strike in the Finale)

segments.t: To avoid paying the massive contract fine, Viktor Petrovich returns to the studio stage for the final round—but stages a quiet protest. While his opponent Oksana busily prepares her dish, Barinov leans against his station reading a newspaper, pointing out that his contract says he must appear on camera, not cook. Let's listen to their clash in Russian.
Это финал, и пусть победит сильнейший!
Стоп, что там у нас происходит?
Тихо, ребята, я сейчас сам разберусь.
Витя, ты что сейчас тут творишь?
По договору я должен только сниматься.
Вот я честно стою и снимаюсь.
А готовить я сегодня не буду.
По какому ещё договору, ты слышишь?
Быстро готовь тут любое блюдо!
А потом иди на все четыре стороны!
Угадай, какой палец у меня в кармане?
Дима, давай сегодня только без скандалов.
Now let's examine Chef Barinov's clever on-stage protest in the finale line by line.
Это финал, и пусть победит сильнейший!
'This is the finale, and may the strongest win!' Nagiyev speaks up evenly in this moment, grounding the moment in plain reality.
Стоп, что там у нас происходит?
'Stop, what is going on over there?' Nagiyev quizzes calmly how Barinov expects that to work in practice.
Тихо, ребята, я сейчас сам разберусь.
'Quiet, guys, I will handle this myself right now.' Nagiyev underscores one key word with Barinov: "rebyata" means "the boys, the lads", and it carries the main weight of what Nagiyev is saying.
Витя, ты что сейчас тут творишь?
'Vitya, what are you doing right here?' Nagiyev frames the thought calmly now: the "-sya" ending on "seychas" ("now") turns the action inward or makes it happen between people naturally.
По договору я должен только сниматься.
'According to the contract I only have to appear on camera.' Barinov reacts candidly without any doubt, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
Вот я честно стою и снимаюсь.
'So here I am honestly standing and being filmed.' Barinov favors one vivid detail right here: "snimayus" means "act", and it carries the main weight of what Barinov is saying.
А готовить я сегодня не буду.
'But I am not going to cook today.' Barinov speaks up wryly with a shrug, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
По какому ещё договору, ты слышишь?
'According to what contract, do you hear me?' Nagiyev presses bluntly before Barinov can change the subject.
Быстро готовь тут любое блюдо!
'Quickly cook any dish right here!' Nagiyev highlights one colorful piece in reply: "lyuboye" means "any" (from "lyuboy"), giving the line its exact edge.
А потом иди на все четыре стороны!
'And then go wherever you please!' Nagiyev replies steadily to settle things, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
Угадай, какой палец у меня в кармане?
'Guess which finger is in my pocket?' Barinov asks sharply if there is more going on behind the scenes.
Дима, давай сегодня только без скандалов.
'Dima, let's just have no scandals today.' Barinov sharpens one pointed element on cue: "skandalov" means "scandal, fuss" (from "skandal"), giving the line its exact edge.

Nagiyev is furious at Barinov's loophole, while the producer begs Nagiyev not to ruin the broadcast with a brawl. Listen for the words meaning finale, contract, and scandals. See you next time!
Хорошего дня!
